record.paper_title: Open Problems on Eigenvalues of the Laplacian
record.original_question: For Dirichlet Laplacian eigenvalues on bounded domains Ω ⊂ ℝⁿ, do the next-level analogues of the Faber-Krahn-type inequalities hold—namely Aλ₅ ≥ (Aλ₅)_disk, A(λ₄+λ₅) ≥ [A(λ₄+λ₅)]_disk, |Ω|^{2/n} λ_{n(n+3)/2} ≥ (|Ω|^{2/n} λ_{n(n+3)/2})_{n-ball}, and |Ω|^{2/n}(λₙ₊₂ + ··· + λ_{n(n+3)/2}) ≥ the corresponding n-ball value? More generally, for each k ≥ 3, what is the optimal lower bound for |Ω|^{2/n} λ_k, and which domain or limiting family of domains attains it?

evidence.quote: Analogous, but even more tenuous conjectures would be Aλ₅ ≥ (Aλ₅)|disk, A(λ₄ + λ₅) ≥ [A(λ₄ + λ₅)]|disk, |Ω|^{2/n} λ_{n(n+3)/2} ≥ (|Ω|^{2/n} λ_{n(n+3)/2})|n-ball, and |Ω|^{2/n}(λₙ₊₂ + ··· + λ_{n(n+3)/2}) ≥ [|Ω|^{2/n}(λₙ₊₂ + ··· + λ_{n(n+3)/2})]|n-ball. Thus, in general it is an open problem to find the optimal lower bound to |Ω|^{2/n} λ_k for k ≥ 3 and to discover the shape of domain that saturates it.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let Ω ⊂ ℝⁿ be a bounded open domain, and let 0 < λ₁(Ω) ≤ λ₂(Ω) ≤ λ₃(Ω) ≤ ⋯ denote the eigenvalues (counted with multiplicity) of the Dirichlet Laplacian on Ω, i.e. the values λ for which there exists a nonzero u ∈ H₀¹(Ω) with −Δu = λu in Ω and u = 0 on ∂Ω. Let |Ω| denote the Lebesgue measure of Ω, and in the planar case (n = 2) write A = |Ω|. For each k ≥ 1, let (·)_{n-ball} denote the value of the corresponding scale-invariant functional evaluated on a Euclidean ball in ℝⁿ (in the planar case, a disk).

Address the following questions.

(a) In the planar case n = 2, does the inequality
    A · λ₅(Ω) ≥ (A · λ₅)_{disk}
hold for every bounded planar domain Ω, with equality only when Ω is a disk?

(b) In the planar case n = 2, does
    A · (λ₄(Ω) + λ₅(Ω)) ≥ [A · (λ₄ + λ₅)]_{disk}
hold for every bounded planar domain Ω?

(c) For every n ≥ 2 and every bounded domain Ω ⊂ ℝⁿ, does
    |Ω|^{2/n} · λ_{n(n+3)/2}(Ω) ≥ ( |Ω|^{2/n} · λ_{n(n+3)/2} )_{n-ball}
hold?

(d) For every n ≥ 2 and every bounded domain Ω ⊂ ℝⁿ, does
    |Ω|^{2/n} · ( λ_{n+2}(Ω) + λ_{n+3}(Ω) + ⋯ + λ_{n(n+3)/2}(Ω) ) ≥ [ |Ω|^{2/n} · ( λ_{n+2} + ⋯ + λ_{n(n+3)/2} ) ]_{n-ball}
hold?

(e) More generally, for each integer k ≥ 3 and each dimension n ≥ 2, determine the sharp constant
    C_{n,k} := inf_{Ω ⊂ ℝⁿ bounded} |Ω|^{2/n} λ_k(Ω),
and identify the domain (or limiting family of domains, possibly disconnected or degenerate) that attains this infimum.
artifact.category_tag: Faber-Krahn inequalities for higher Dirichlet eigenvalues
artifact.status_search_result: The sharp lower bound for |Ω|^{2/n} λ_k for k ≥ 3 and the optimizing shapes are known only in special cases. The classical Faber–Krahn theorem handles k = 1, and Krahn–Szegő settled k = 2 (two equal balls). For k ≥ 3 the optimizers in ℝⁿ are not generally known; partial results exist (e.g. via Bucur–Mazzoleni–Pratelli existence theory and numerical work), but the explicit conjectured inequalities for λ₅, λ₄+λ₅, λ_{n(n+3)/2}, and the corresponding sums remain open.

status_evidence.title: Faber-Krahn inequality for polygons
status_evidence.snippet: the problem of eigenvalue optimization ... for higher eigenvalues remains far from fully understood
status_evidence.claim: Higher-eigenvalue Faber-Krahn-type optimization problems remain largely open.

status_evidence.title: Dirichlet eigenvalue - Encyclopedia of Mathematics
status_evidence.snippet: Faber-Krahn: ball minimizes the first Dirichlet eigenvalue among domains of given volume
status_evidence.claim: Only the k=1 case is classically resolved; k≥3 optimizers are not generally known.
